privacy.title: Your counter stays on your device
privacy.body: Hinge Counter stores daily recorded opening totals by source (foreground sensor, Shortcuts or manual), dates and your counting preference in the app sandbox. The app does not send these records to the developer. It has no accounts, advertising, tracking or third-party analytics SDKs.

privacy.title: Hinge observations
privacy.body: On supported hardware, the app uses live hinge observations while an app scene is active. Angle and observation timing are processed locally to recognize a close-to-open movement. Raw angle samples are not saved in your history. Missed openings during lock, suspension or use of another app are not reconstructed.

privacy.title: Widgets, backups and exports
privacy.body: The app shares a copy of saved totals with its own widget extension through an App Group on this device. Your operating-system backup settings may include app data. CSV and JSON files leave the app only when you choose an export or sharing destination. Those services process your files under their own policies.

privacy.title: Retention and deletion
privacy.body: Records remain until you erase them, replace them by restoring a backup, or remove the app and its data. Settings > Erase all counts clears the in-app history and attempts to replace the widget snapshot; check the widget status afterward. Copies in device backups, exported files, a destination service or a previously rendered widget are not remotely erased. Manage those copies with the relevant system or service.

privacy.title: Support and external websites
privacy.body: Opening a support or privacy link hands the URL to your browser. GitHub hosts this website and the public issue tracker and may process connection information under its own privacy statement. If you file an issue, information you choose to submit is public and processed by GitHub. Do not include backups, personal identifiers or private information. The app never uploads a support report automatically.

privacy.title: Contact and changes
privacy.body: Contact the project maintainer through the linked GitHub issue tracker with non-sensitive questions. This policy applies to the functionality described here. We will update it when that functionality or data handling changes.

support.title: Why does the count miss openings?
support.body: The foreground sensor needs a supported hinge and a complete close-to-open movement while the app is active. Switching apps, locking the phone or a display handoff can interrupt it. In Shortcuts mode, only runs of the Record Opening action count. Check that counting is enabled and your opening automation is turned on. Neither method can recover earlier missed openings.

support.title: How do I count while using another app?
support.body: On iPhone Duo with iOS 27.2 or later, choose Settings > Counting method > Shortcuts and turn on Shortcuts counting. If Settings offers Add opening automation, tap it and choose Shortcuts. If Files opens, save Count iPhone Duo Openings and tap the file in Files. Add the shortcut, turn on its opening automation and allow immediate runs. Keep only one opening automation enabled. For manual setup, open Hinge Counter’s page in Shortcuts. Touch and hold Record Opening and choose New Shortcut. In the editor, tap Search if the action library is hidden. Choose Automation, select the iPhone opening trigger and Opened only, and allow immediate runs. If the trigger is missing in Shortcuts, you can use the foreground sensor while Hinge Counter is open. Running the action by hand also adds an entry.

support.title: What counts as one opening?
support.body: The foreground sensor requires an observed angle of 10 degrees or less followed by 170 degrees or more, at least 0.35 seconds apart. Partial folds do not rearm it. Shortcuts uses the opening trigger defined by iOS and records each action run separately.

support.title: Can I see history older than 90 days?
support.body: Yes. Choose History > All to see every saved date. The chart groups longer spans into monthly or yearly totals, and Show older days reveals earlier daily records. Days without a saved record are omitted from the All daily list. Records do not expire after 90 days. Erasing history, restoring a replacement backup, or removing app data can remove records, so keep a JSON backup for a separate copy.

support.title: Why does my widget look old?
support.body: Widgets show saved snapshots and iOS controls refresh timing. They do not keep hinge monitoring alive. Open the app, check Settings > Widgets for a sharing error, and allow iOS to refresh. During testing, the app and extension must have matching App Group signing. Choose separate all-time, today, this week or this month widgets. Weeks follow the device’s first day of the week; months use Gregorian local dates. Current periods include saved dates through today. Historical manual entries remain included and labeled.

support.title: Back up, restore or erase
support.body: In Settings, export a JSON backup before replacing or erasing history. CSV is for reading daily totals, not restoring. Restore replaces history; it does not merge it. If storage fails, counting pauses: retry saving or loading, or export the original file for your own recovery. Never post that file publicly.

support.title: Report a problem
support.body: Use the public GitHub issue tracker below. Include the app version, operating-system version, device model, reproducible steps and whether the app was active. Remove personal information from screenshots. There is no need to upload your counter backup.
